name: Chapter 9: Straight Lines
description: Slope, angle between lines, forms of a line, distance formulas, concurrency, images and reflections, families of lines.

cards.term: Distance between P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂)?
Section formula (internal, ratio m : n)?
cards.definition: \(\left(\dfrac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m+n},\ \dfrac{my_2 + ny_1}{m+n}\right)\). Midpoint: m = n

cards.term: Area of the triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃)?
cards.definition: \(\dfrac12\left|x_1(y_2-y_3) + x_2(y_3-y_1) + x_3(y_1-y_2)\right|\). Area = 0 ⟺ points are collinear

cards.term: Distance between (6, −4) and (3, 0)? Area of (4,4), (3,−2), (−3,16)?
cards.definition: 5; area 27 (½|4(−18) + 3(12) + (−3)(6)| = ½·54)

cards.term: Centroid of a triangle? Which other points are asked?
cards.definition: Centroid ((x₁+x₂+x₃)/3, (y₁+y₂+y₃)/3). Also: incentre ((ax₁ + bx₂ + cx₃)/(a+b+c), …), circumcentre (equidistant from vertices), orthocentre (meet of altitudes)

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q1: area of the quadrilateral (−4,5), (0,7), (5,−5), (−4,−2)?
cards.definition: Shoelace: ½|−28 − 35 − 30 − 28| = 60.5

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q2: equilateral triangle, side 2a, base along the y-axis with midpoint at the origin. Vertices?
cards.definition: (0, a), (0, −a), (√3a, 0) (or (−√3a, 0) as the third vertex)

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q3: distance PQ when PQ ∥ y-axis; when PQ ∥ x-axis?
cards.definition: |y₂ − y₁| and |x₂ − x₁|

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q4: a point on the x-axis equidistant from (7, 6) and (3, 4)?
Define the inclination and slope of a line.
cards.definition: Inclination θ = angle the line makes with the positive x-axis, measured anticlockwise, 0° ≤ θ < 180°. Slope m = tan θ (θ ≠ 90°)

cards.term: Slope of the x-axis, of a horizontal line, of a vertical line?
cards.definition: 0, 0, undefined (θ = 90°)

cards.term: Slope as tan of the inclination
cards.definition: m = tan θ for inclination 0 ≤ θ < 180°, θ ≠ 90°: 0 at 0°, 1 at 45°, undefined at 90°, −1 at 135°; positive for acute, negative for obtuse

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Slope · inclination

A line turns anticlockwise from 0° to 180°. How does its slope m = tan θ change?

Picture tan θ as θ sweeps from 0° to 180°.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Slope · inclination

A line turns anticlockwise from 0° to 180°. How does its slope m = tan θ change?

θ = 0°: m = 0. Rising to 45°: m = 1. At 90° the line is vertical: slope undefined. Past 90° the slope jumps to −∞ and rises through −1 (135°) back to 0.

So: acute angle → positive slope; obtuse angle → negative slope. Slope of the x-axis is 0; of the y-axis undefined.

cards.term: Slope of the line through (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂)?
cards.definition: \(m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), x₁ ≠ x₂ (if x₁ = x₂ the line is vertical)
−3/2; 0; undefined; √3

cards.term: Condition for two non-vertical lines to be parallel? Perpendicular?
cards.definition: m₁ = m₂ (parallel); m₁m₂ = −1 (perpendicular: negative reciprocals)

cards.term: Why is m₁m₂ = −1 for perpendicular lines?
cards.definition: β = α + 90° → tan β = −cot α = −1/tan α. A 90° turn sends slope m to −1/m (e.g. 2 → −½)

cards.term: Condition for three points A, B, C to be collinear?
cards.definition: slope AB = slope BC (or area of ABC = 0)

cards.term: Angle between two lines with slopes m₁ and m₂?
cards.definition: \(\tan\theta = \left|\dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{1 + m_1m_2}\right|\) (acute angle); if 1 + m₁m₂ = 0 the lines are perpendicular

cards.term: Example 2: two lines at 45° to a line of slope 1/2
cards.definition: tan θ = |(m1−m2)/(1+m1 m2)|; with m1=1/2 and θ=45° the other slope is 3 or −1/3 (one line on each side)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Angle between lines · two answers

One line has slope ½. Another makes an angle of 45° with it. Find the other slope.

The modulus in the angle formula gives ± cases.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Angle between lines · two answers

One line has slope ½. Another makes an angle of 45° with it. Find the other slope.

tan 45° = |(m − ½)/(1 + m/2)| = 1 ⇒ (m − ½) = ±(1 + m/2) ⇒ m = 3 or m = −⅓.

Two lines lie at 45° on either side of the given one. The acute angle formula tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| has a modulus, so it always gives two solutions when θ is known.

cards.term: Example 3: line through (−2, 6), (4, 8) ⟂ line through (8, 12), (x, 24). Find x.
cards.definition: m₁ = 1/3, m₂ = 12/(x − 8) → product −1 → x − 8 = −36 → x = −28

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q5: slope of the line through the origin and the midpoint of (0, −4) and (8, 0)?
cards.definition: Midpoint (4, −2): slope −1/2

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q6: show (4, 4), (3, 5), (−1, −1) form a right triangle without Pythagoras.
cards.definition: Slope of (4,4)→(3,5) is −1; slope of (4,4)→(−1,−1) is 1; product −1, so the right angle is at (4, 4)

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q7: slope of a line making 30° with the positive y-axis (anticlockwise)?
cards.definition: Inclination = 90° + 30° = 120° → m = tan 120° = −√3

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q8: show (−2,−1), (4,0), (3,3), (−3,2) form a parallelogram using slopes.
cards.definition: AB and DC both have slope 1/6; BC and AD both have slope −3. Opposite sides parallel ✓

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q9: angle between the x-axis and the line through (3, −1) and (4, −2)?
cards.definition: m = −1 → inclination 135° (angle with the axis 45°)

cards.term: Ex 9.1 Q10: one slope is double the other; tan of the angle between them is 1/3. Slopes?
cards.definition: |m|/(1 + 2m²) = 1/3 → 2m² − 3|m| + 1 = 0 → (1, 2) or (½, 1) (or their negatives)

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q8: angle between √3x + y = 1 and x + √3y = 1.
Ex 9.3 Q9: line through (h, 3), (4, 1) is ⟂ to 7x − 9y − 19 = 0. Find h.
cards.definition: Slope needed −9/7: (1 − 3)/(4 − h) = −9/7 → h = 22/9

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q11: two lines through (2, 3) meet at 60°; one has slope 2. The other?
cards.definition: |(m − 2)/(1 + 2m)| = √3 → m = −(8 + 5√3)/11 or m = (5√3 − 8)/11 (two lines, one each side)

cards.term: Misc Q18: y = 3x + 1 and 2y = x + 3 are equally inclined to y = mx + 4. Find m.
cards.definition: Equal angles: |(m − 3)/(1 + 3m)| = |(m − ½)/(1 + m/2)|; the non-trivial case gives 7m² − 2m − 7 = 0 → m = (1 ± 5√2)/7

cards.term: Misc Q12: line through the origin at angle θ to y = mx + c?
cards.definition: y = ((m ± tan θ)/(1 ∓ m tan θ)) x

cards.term: Horizontal and vertical lines at distance a from the axes?
cards.definition: Horizontal: y = ±a; vertical: x = ±b

cards.term: Example 4: lines through (−2, 3) parallel to the axes?
cards.definition: y = 3 (∥ x-axis) and x = −2 (∥ y-axis)

cards.term: Forms of the equation of a line
cards.definition: Point–slope: through (x₀, y₀), slope m: y − y₀ = m(x − x₀); Two-point: through (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂): y − y₁ = ((y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁))(x − x₁); Slope–intercept: slope m, y-intercept c: y = mx + c; Slope with x-intercept d: y = m(x − d); Intercept form: intercepts a, b: x/a + y/b = 1; General form: Ax + By + C = 0  (A, B not both 0)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
9.3 · Forms of a line

Write the equation.

Point–slope: through (x₀, y₀), slope m?
Two-point: through (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂)?
Slope–intercept: slope m, y-intercept c?
Slope with x-intercept d?
Intercept form: intercepts a, b?
General form?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
9.3 · Forms of a line

Write the equation.

Point–slope: through (x₀, y₀), slope my − y₀ = m(x − x₀)
Two-point: through (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂)y − y₁ = ((y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁))(x − x₁)
Slope–intercept: slope m, y-intercept cy = mx + c
Slope with x-intercept dy = m(x − d)
Intercept form: intercepts a, bx/a + y/b = 1
General formAx + By + C = 0 (A, B not both 0)

cards.term: Slope and intercepts from Ax + By + C = 0?
cards.definition: Slope −A/B; y-intercept −C/B; x-intercept −C/A

cards.term: Example 5: line through (−2, 3) with slope −4.
cards.definition: y − 3 = −4(x + 2) → 4x + y + 5 = 0

cards.term: Example 6: line through (1, −1) and (3, 5).
cards.definition: slope 3: y + 1 = 3(x − 1) → 3x − y − 4 = 0 (NCERT writes −3x + y + 4 = 0)

cards.term: Example 7: tan θ = ½ with (i) y-intercept −3/2 (ii) x-intercept 4.
cards.definition: (i) y = x/2 − 3/2 → x − 2y − 3 = 0 (ii) y = (x − 4)/2 → x − 2y − 4 = 0

cards.term: Example 8: intercepts −3 and 2.
cards.definition: x/(−3) + y/2 = 1 → 2x − 3y + 6 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q1–3: equations of the axes; through (−4, 3) with slope ½; through the origin with slope m.
cards.definition: y = 0 and x = 0; y − 3 = (x + 4)/2 → x − 2y + 10 = 0; y = mx

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q5–6: x-intercept 3 units left of the origin, slope −2; y-intercept 2 above the origin at 30°.
cards.definition: 2x + y + 6 = 0; y = x/√3 + 2 → x − √3y + 2√3 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q7: line through (−1, 1) and (2, −4).
cards.definition: slope −5/3 → 5x + 3y + 2 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q8: median through R in triangle P(2,1), Q(−2,3), R(4,5).
cards.definition: Midpoint of PQ = (0, 2); slope (5 − 2)/4 = 3/4 → 3x − 4y + 8 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q9: through (−3, 5) ⟂ the line through (2, 5) and (−3, 6).
cards.definition: That slope is −1/5, so use 5: y − 5 = 5(x + 3) → 5x − y + 20 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q10: a line ⟂ to the segment (1,0)–(2,3) divides it 1 : n. Equation?
cards.definition: Point ((n + 2)/(n + 1), 3/(n + 1)), slope −1/3: (n + 1)x + 3(n + 1)y = n + 11

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q11: equal intercepts, through (2, 3).
cards.definition: x + y = a with 2 + 3 = a → x + y = 5

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q12: through (2, 2), sum of intercepts 9.
cards.definition: 2/a + 2/(9 − a) = 1 → a² − 9a + 18 = 0 → a = 3 or 6: 2x + y = 6 and x + 2y = 6

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q13: through (0, 2) at 2π/3; and the parallel line 2 units below the origin.
cards.definition: slope −√3: √3x + y − 2 = 0 and √3x + y + 2 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q14: the perpendicular from the origin meets the line at (−2, 9). Equation?
cards.definition: Normal direction (−2, 9): −2(x + 2) + 9(y − 9) = 0 → 2x − 9y + 85 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q15: L is linear in C: L = 124.942 at 20°C and 125.134 at 110°C. Find L(C).
cards.definition: slope 0.192/90: L = 0.00213C + 124.899 (approx)

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q16: 980 L sold at ₹14, 1220 L at ₹16 (linear). Demand at ₹17?
cards.definition: Slope 120 L per rupee: 980 + 120·3 = 1340 litres

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q17–18: midpoint (a, b) of a segment between the axes; point (h, k) dividing it 1 : 2.
cards.definition: Intercepts 2a, 2b: x/a + y/b = 2. Second: 2kx + hy = 3hk

cards.term: Ex 9.2 Q19: show (3, 0), (−2, −2), (8, 2) are collinear.
cards.definition: Slope of the first two: 2/5; slope of the first and third: 2/5 → same line ✓

cards.term: Method: which form of a line to use?
cards.definition: Slope + point → point–slope. Two points → two-point (or find slope). Intercepts → x/a + y/b = 1. Normal direction known → A(x − x₁) + B(y − y₁) = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q1: slope–intercept form of x + 7y = 0, 6x + 3y − 5 = 0, y = 0.
Ex 9.3 Q2: intercept form of 3x + 2y − 12 = 0, 4x − 3y = 6, 3y + 2 = 0.
cards.definition: x/4 + y/6 = 1 (4, 6); x/(3/2) + y/(−2) = 1 (3/2, −2); y = −2/3: y-intercept −2/3, no x-intercept

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q6–7: ∥ to 3x − 4y + 2 = 0 through (−2, 3); ⟂ to x − 7y + 5 = 0 with x-intercept 3.
cards.definition: 3x − 4y + 18 = 0; slope −7: y = −7(x − 3) → 7x + y − 21 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q10: the line through (x₁, y₁) parallel to Ax + By + C = 0?
cards.definition: A(x − x₁) + B(y − y₁) = 0: same A, B (same direction), new constant. Perpendicular: B(x − x₁) − A(y − y₁) = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q12: right bisector of (3, 4) and (−1, 2).
cards.definition: Midpoint (1, 3), slope of segment ½ → perpendicular slope −2: 2x + y − 5 = 0

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q14: the perpendicular from the origin to y = mx + c meets it at (−1, 2). m and c?
cards.definition: Origin-to-point slope −2 = −1/m → m = ½, c = 2 + m = 5/2

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q16: altitude from A(2, 3) in the triangle A, B(4, −1), C(1, 2): equation and length.
cards.definition: BC has slope −1 (x + y = 3), so the altitude has slope 1: x − y + 1 = 0; length = |2 + 3 − 3|/√2 = √2

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q17: p = perpendicular from the origin to the line with intercepts a, b. Show 1/p² = 1/a² + 1/b².
cards.definition: Line bx + ay = ab: p = ab/√(a² + b²) → 1/p² = (a² + b²)/(a²b²) = 1/a² + 1/b² ✓

cards.term: Distance of the point (x₁, y₁) from the line Ax + By + C = 0?
Distance from a point to a line
cards.definition: d = |Ax1+By1+C|/√(A²+B²); origin to 3x+4y−10=0 is 2 with foot (6/5, 8/5)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Distance of a point from a line

Find the distance of the origin from 3x + 4y − 10 = 0 and the foot of the perpendicular.

Which quantity goes in the numerator?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Distance of a point from a line

Find the distance of the origin from 3x + 4y − 10 = 0 and the foot of the perpendicular.

d = |Ax₁ + By₁ + C| / √(A² + B²) = |0 + 0 − 10|/5 = 2.

Foot: move from O along the normal (3, 4)/5 by 2 → (6/5, 8/5). Check: 3(6/5) + 4(8/5) = 10 ✓.

Trap: the absolute value, and √(A² + B²) not A² + B².

cards.term: Distance between parallel lines Ax + By + C₁ = 0 and Ax + By + C₂ = 0?
cards.definition: \(d = \dfrac{|C_1 - C_2|}{\sqrt{A^2 + B^2}}\) (first make the A, B identical in both)

cards.term: Trap: distance between 3x + 4y + 5 = 0 and 6x + 8y − 10 = 0.
cards.definition: Divide the second by 2: 3x + 4y − 5 = 0. Then d = |5 − (−5)|/5 = 2

cards.term: Example 9: distance of (3, −5) from 3x − 4y − 26 = 0.
cards.definition: |9 + 20 − 26|/5 = 3/5

cards.term: Example 10: distance between 3x − 4y + 7 = 0 and 3x − 4y + 5 = 0.
cards.definition: |7 − 5|/5 = 2/5

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q3: distance of (−1, 1) from 12(x + 6) = 5(y − 2).
Ex 9.3 Q4: points on the x-axis at distance 4 from x/3 + y/4 = 1.
Ex 9.3 Q5: distance between 15x + 8y − 34 = 0 and 15x + 8y + 31 = 0; and between l(x + y) + p = 0 and l(x + y) − r = 0.
cards.definition: 65/17 = 65/17; |p + r|/(|l|√2) = |p + r|/(|l|√2)

cards.term: Ex 9.3 Q13: foot of the perpendicular from (−1, 3) to 3x − 4y − 16 = 0.
Ex 9.3 Q15: p, q are perpendiculars from the origin to x cos θ − y sin θ = k cos 2θ and x sec θ + y cosec θ = k. Show p² + 4q² = k².
cards.definition: p = |k cos 2θ|; q = k/√(sec²θ + cosec²θ) = k sinθ cosθ = (k/2) sin 2θ. Then p² + 4q² = k²(cos²2θ + sin²2θ) = k² ✓

cards.term: Misc Q3: points on the y-axis at distance 4 from x/3 + y/4 = 1.
Misc Q4: perpendicular distance from the origin to the line joining (cos θ, sin θ) and (cos φ, sin φ).
cards.definition: |cos((θ − φ)/2)| (a chord of the unit circle)

cards.term: Misc Q20: the line equidistant from the parallels 9x + 6y − 7 = 0 and 3x + 2y + 6 = 0.
cards.definition: Rewrite the second as 9x + 6y + 18 = 0. Middle constant: (−7 + 18)/2 = 11/2 → 18x + 12y + 11 = 0

cards.term: Misc Q22: product of the perpendiculars from (±√(a² − b²), 0) to x cos θ/a + y sin θ/b = 1.
cards.definition: Multiply the two distances: the denominators combine to (cos²θ/a² + sin²θ/b²) and the numerators to 1 − (a² − b²)cos²θ/a² = b²(cos²θ/a² + sin²θ/b²). The product is b²

cards.term: Three lines are concurrent. What does that mean and how do you test it?
cards.definition: They pass through one point. Solve two, then check the third; or the 3×3 determinant of coefficients = 0

cards.term: Example 11: 2x + y − 3 = 0, 5x + ky − 3 = 0, 3x − y − 2 = 0 are concurrent. Find k.
cards.definition: Lines 1 and 3 meet at (1, 1); it must satisfy the second: 5 + k − 3 = 0 → k = −2

cards.term: Misc Q8: 3x + y − 2 = 0, px + 2y − 3 = 0, 2x − y − 3 = 0 meet at one point. p?
cards.definition: Lines 1 and 3 meet at (1, −1): p − 2 − 3 = 0 → p = 5

cards.term: Misc Q9: y = m₁x + c₁ etc. concurrent ⟹ m₁(c₂ − c₃) + m₂(c₃ − c₁) + m₃(c₁ − c₂) = 0. Idea?
cards.definition: Concurrency ⟺ determinant |m₁ −1 c₁; m₂ −1 c₂; m₃ −1 c₃| = 0; expanding gives the identity

cards.term: Family of lines through the intersection of L₁ = 0 and L₂ = 0?
cards.definition: L₁ + λL₂ = 0 (λ a parameter). Choose λ using an extra condition, e.g. passing through a given point

cards.term: Misc Q11: through the intersection of 4x + 7y − 3 = 0 and 2x − 3y + 1 = 0 with equal intercepts.
cards.definition: Intersection (1/13, 5/13). Equal intercepts: x + y = k with k = 6/13 → 13x + 13y = 6

cards.term: Misc Q5: line ∥ the y-axis through the intersection of x − 7y + 5 = 0 and 3x + y = 0.
cards.definition: y = −3x → x + 21x + 5 = 0 → x = −5/22: 22x + 5 = 0

cards.term: Misc Q1: (k − 3)x − (4 − k²)y + k² − 7k + 6 = 0 is (a) ∥ x-axis (b) ∥ y-axis (c) through the origin.
cards.definition: (a) coefficient of x = 0 → k = 3 (b) coefficient of y = 0 → k = ±2 (c) constant = 0 → k² − 7k + 6 = 0 → k = 1, 6

cards.term: Misc Q2: intercepts with sum 1 and product −6.
cards.definition: (a, b) = (3, −2) or (−2, 3): 2x − 3y = 6 and 3x − 2y + 6 = 0

cards.term: Misc Q7: area of the triangle formed by y = x, y = −x, x = k.
cards.definition: Vertices (0,0), (k,k), (k,−k): k²

cards.term: Example 14: area of the triangle from y = m₁x + c₁, y = m₂x + c₂, x = 0.
cards.definition: (c₁ − c₂)² / (2|m₁ − m₂|)

cards.term: Example 15: a line whose segment between 5x − y + 4 = 0 and 3x + 4y − 4 = 0 is bisected at (1, 5).
cards.definition: Endpoints (α₁, 5α₁ + 4), (α₂, (4 − 3α₂)/4) with α₁ + α₂ = 2 gives α₁ = 26/23: 107x − 3y − 92 = 0

cards.term: Example 16: path of a point equidistant from 3x − 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 5.
cards.definition: Equal distances give k = 0 or h = 5/3: the angle bisectors y = 0 and x = 5/3, both straight lines

cards.term: Angle bisectors of a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0?
cards.definition: (a₁x + b₁y + c₁)/√(a₁² + b₁²) = ±(a₂x + b₂y + c₂)/√(a₂² + b₂²): two perpendicular bisectors (make c₁, c₂ same sign to pick the one containing the origin)

cards.term: Misc Q19: the sum of the distances of P(x, y) from x + y − 5 = 0 and 3x − 2y + 7 = 0 is always 10. Locus?
cards.definition: Removing the modulus in each region gives a linear equation, so P moves on a line (segment)

cards.term: Misc Q23: a person at the meeting point of 2x − 3y + 4 = 0 and 3x + 4y − 5 = 0 wants to reach 6x − 7y + 8 = 0 fastest.
cards.definition: The shortest path is the perpendicular from (−1/17, 22/17): 119x + 102y − 125 = 0

cards.term: Reflection of a point in a line (Example 13)
cards.definition: Image Q of P(1,2) in x−3y+4=0: PQ ⟂ line and midpoint on line; formula (x′−x1)/A=(y′−y1)/B=−2(Ax1+By1+C)/(A²+B²); Q=(6/5,7/5)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Image in a line (mirror)

Find the image of P(1, 2) in the line x − 3y + 4 = 0.

Use “perpendicular” and “midpoint on the line”.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Image in a line (mirror)

Find the image of P(1, 2) in the line x − 3y + 4 = 0.

The line is the perpendicular bisector of PQ. Two conditions: (i) PQ ⟂ line (slope of PQ = −3); (ii) the midpoint of PQ lies on the line.

Shortcut: (x′ − x₁)/A = (y′ − y₁)/B = −2(Ax₁ + By₁ + C)/(A² + B²). Here −2(−1)/10 = 0.2 → Q = (1 + 0.2, 2 − 0.6) = (6/5, 7/5).

cards.term: Light reflection: use the image point
cards.definition: Reflect the target in the mirror line; the light path is the straight line to the image: A(13/5,0) for (1,2)→x-axis→(5,3)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Reflection of light · Misc Q21

A ray from (1, 2) reflects on the x-axis at A and passes through (5, 3). Find A.

Where would the ray go if the mirror were not there?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Reflection of light · Misc Q21

A ray from (1, 2) reflects on the x-axis at A and passes through (5, 3). Find A.

Reflect (5, 3) in the x-axis to (5, −3). The reflected ray appears to come from the image, so A lies on the straight line from (1, 2) to (5, −3).

Slope = −5/4: y − 2 = −(5/4)(x − 1); set y = 0: x = 1 + 8/5 = 13/5. A = (13/5, 0).

cards.term: Reflection of (x₁, y₁) in Ax + By + C = 0?
cards.definition: \(\dfrac{x^{\prime}-x_1}{A} = \dfrac{y^{\prime}-y_1}{B} = \dfrac{-2(Ax_1 + By_1 + C)}{A^2 + B^2}\)

cards.term: Misc Q17: image of (3, 8) in x + 3y = 7.
Reflection of (a, b) in the axes and in y = x, y = −x?

cards.definition: (−1 + 3cos θ) + (2 + 3sin θ) = 4 → cos θ + sin θ = 1 → θ = 0° or 90° (horizontal or vertical line)

cards.definition: Slopes −2/3 and 3/2: product −1 → (b)

cards.term:
MCQ: If the points (1, 2), (3, 4), (k, 6) are collinear, k =
(a) 4 (b) 5 (c) 6 (d) 3
cards.definition: Slope 1: (6 − 2)/(k − 1) = 1 → (a) 4

cards.definition: 60° − 45° = (a) 15°

Assertion–Reason.
A: The slope of the y-axis is not defined.
R: The y-axis makes an angle of 90° with the x-axis and tan 90° is not defined.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not explain A (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: If m₁m₂ = −1 the lines are perpendicular.
R: tan θ = |(m₁ − m₂)/(1 + m₁m₂)| is undefined when m₁m₂ = −1.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a): the angle is 90°

cards.term: True/False: the lines x − 2y = 3 and 2x − 4y = 7 are perpendicular.
cards.definition: False: both have slope ½, so they are parallel

cards.term: 3-mark: find the equation of the line through (2, 3) making equal intercepts on the axes.
cards.definition: x + y = 5 (and y = (3/2)x through the origin has intercepts 0, 0 if allowed). Standard answer x + y = 5

cards.term: 4-mark: find the foot of the perpendicular from (1, 2) to x + y − 5 = 0 and the image.
cards.definition: Ax₁ + By₁ + C = −2, so t = −2/2 = −1: foot = (1 + 1, 2 + 1) = (2, 3); image = (3, 4)

cards.term: Case-based: a road passes through A(0, 0) and B(4, 3). A well is at W(5, 0). Shortest distance from W to the road?
cards.definition: Road: 3x − 4y = 0; d = |15|/5 = 3 units
